title: "install.packages() on a local archive crashed inside a renv project"

categories: [renv and installation]

versions: "Observed in 2022 with R 4.1 and {renv}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2022)"
---

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
install.packages("~/bee2_0.0.1.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

```text
Installing package into '/home/florence/sunglasses/renv/library/R-4.1/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu'
(as 'lib' is unspecified)
Error in startsWith(contriburl, "file:") : non-character object(s)
```
:::

This pitfall depends on a {renv} project and a package archive on disk, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

With `repos = NULL`, `install.packages()` is supposed to install the given file directly. In this {renv} project, though, the call ended up in the part of the code that handles repositories: `contrib.url(NULL)` does not return text, and `startsWith()` refuses anything that is not text.

The message mentions `contriburl`, an argument the user never passed. Nothing suggests that the problem comes from installing a local file in this context.

## The remedy

Go through a function designed to install a local archive, which worked in the same project.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
remotes::install_local("~/bee2_0.0.1.tar.gz")

# or, in a renv project
renv::install("~/bee2_0.0.1.tar.gz")
```
:::
